description: A responsive, self-contained Earth-orbit maneuver workspace with an inertial orbital map, numerical propagation, live telemetry, local-frame instantaneous impulse previews, Hohmann transfer planning, exact next-apsis coasting, circularization planning, flight log, collision detection, playback and zoom controls.
runtime: Vanilla JavaScript ES modules and Canvas 2D; local CSS; no dependencies beyond the provided Vite test build. No runtime network, storage, backend or cross-frame communication.

numericalAssumptions: Planar Newtonian two-body gravity. Fixed Earth gravitational parameter μ = 398600.4418 km³/s²; Earth radius 6371 km. Units: km, seconds, km/s.
Massless spacecraft and spherical, non-rotating Earth. Instantaneous burns in a local outward-radial / counterclockwise-prograde frame.
Fourth-order Runge–Kutta propagation with each internal step no longer than five seconds. Osculating elements are derived directly from position and velocity.
Hohmann preset requires a near-circular counterclockwise orbit (eccentricity ≤ 0.001). Next-apsis time derives from eccentric anomaly and mean anomaly.
limitations: No drag, atmospheric interface, J2/oblateness, third-body gravity, relativity, Earth rotation, thrust duration, fuel budgeting or live ephemerides.
Starting and target altitudes limited to 150–30000 km. Each impulse component is limited to ±4000 m/s; circularization above these limits reports that the proposed burn is partial.

Predicted paths contain up to 421 displayed points and stop at a sampled surface contact. Bound predictions show at most one period or eight hours; escape predictions show six hours. A below-surface osculating periapsis triggers a warning independently of path display.
Playback contact detection is sampled at internal steps of at most five seconds, not a root-solved impact time. Next-apsis coasting is restricted to arrivals within eight hours.

Orbit fitting caps its radial display extent at approximately 92000 km; unbound or very large orbits may extend outside the viewport. Satellite and velocity direction glyphs are enlarged, not physically scaled.
Educational visualization only; not suitable for operational navigation.
repairs: Removed an unnecessary data-URL CSS import to keep the stylesheet fully local.
Throttled moving burn-preview propagation to approximately seven updates per second and reused current-orbit paths for zero-delta previews to reduce unnecessary propagation work.
Added a visible partial-maneuver warning when circularization requires a component beyond the slider limits.
Corrected next-apsis selection at a numerically propagated apoapsis to select the following periapsis rather than the same apoapsis one revolution later. Added dedicated regression checks.
Bounded next-apsis coasting to eight hours to avoid unbounded work on near-escape ellipses.
